# Physics figures as TikZ (based on physicsfigures.com)

Figure based on physicsfigures.com (teacher.dev). Collected for Hari's own teaching use; nothing here has been published. The site's /reuse page states that its example figures are open source under the Apache License 2.0.

## What is in here

| folder / file | content |
|---|---|
| `svg/<gen>/<slug>.svg` | the figure's SVG, downloaded with the site's *Download SVG* button |
| `png/<gen>/<slug>.png` | the preview PNG listed in the sitemap (examples only) |
| `tikz/<gen>/<slug>.tex` (+ `.pdf`) | standalone SVG→TikZ conversion (`\documentclass[tikz,border=2pt]{standalone}`), credit line and source URL in the header |
| `tikz_snippets/<gen>/<slug>.tikz` | just the `tikzpicture` (needs `\usetikzlibrary{arrows.meta}` and the `pf…` colours/`\pffs` macro from the standalone header) |
| `physfig/` | **own parameterised library** `physfig.sty` + `physfig-*.code.tex` (written from scratch, using the site only as a feature list) |
| `OPTIONS.md` | every physfig key: default, allowed values, matching generator control; coverage per generator |
| `repro/<gen>/<slug>.tex` (+ `.pdf`) | each captured figure rebuilt with one physfig macro call |
| `gallery/gallery.pdf` | 8 variations per macro, code shown under each figure |
| `renders/original`, `renders/tikz`, `renders/repro` | PNG renders of the site SVG, the conversion and the macro version |
| `renders/side_by_side`, `renders/triple` | original vs conversion, and original / conversion / macro |
| `contact/contact_sheet.pdf`, `contact/contact_<gen>.png` | contact sheets (original / conversion / macro) |
| `all_figures.tex`, `all_figures.pdf` | every figure (conversion and macro version) with captions, title and source URL |
| `tools/`, `meta.json`, `results.json` | converter and build scripts, capture metadata, per-figure results |

## Using physfig

```latex
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage[T1]{fontenc}
\usepackage{mathptmx}\usepackage[scaled=0.92]{helvet} % optional, close to the site's look
\usepackage{physfig}
\begin{document}
\pfIncline[angle=35, surface=rough, gravity, normal, friction=up]
\pfCircuit[arrangement=parallel, parts={resistor/R_1/4\,\Omega, bulb/L/}, ammeter, switch=open]
\end{document}
```

Put the `physfig/` folder next to your document (or compile with `TEXINPUTS=path/to/physfig//: pdflatex doc.tex`). Needs TikZ, circuitikz (for `\pfCircuit`; load with `[nocircuits]` to skip), xfp and amsmath — all in a standard TeX Live. Macros: `\pfFBD`, `\pfVectors`, `\pfIncline`, `\pfPulley`, `\pfProjectile`, `\pfMotionGraph`, `\pfSpringScale`, `\pfWave`, `\pfCircuit`. A label value `?` gives a blank line for students; `{}` gives no label.

## Counts

| generator | figures (default + examples) | conversions compiled | macro versions compiled |
|---|---|---|---|
| free-body-diagram | 7 (1 + 6) | 7/7 | 7/7 |
| vector-diagram | 6 (1 + 5) | 6/6 | 6/6 |
| inclined-plane | 7 (1 + 6) | 7/7 | 7/7 |
| pulley | 7 (1 + 6) | 7/7 | 7/7 |
| projectile-motion | 6 (1 + 5) | 6/6 | 6/6 |
| motion-graphs | 6 (1 + 5) | 6/6 | 6/6 |
| spring-scale | 6 (1 + 5) | 6/6 | 6/6 |
| waves | 7 (1 + 6) | 7/7 | 7/7 |
| circuit-diagram | 6 (1 + 5) | 6/6 | 6/6 |
| **total** | **58** | **58/58** | **58/58** |

Visual check: every figure was compared side by side (`renders/triple`). The conversions are near-identical to the site's figures (blurred RMSE ≤ 0.10; fonts are Times/Helvetica clones instead of Times New Roman/Arial). The macro versions show the same physics content (same forces, labels, marks, values); layout, scale and spacing are our own, so they are not pixel copies.

## Known imperfections

* Conversions: fonts are mathptmx/Helvetica instead of Times New Roman/Arial; sub/superscript size and offset differ slightly; halo boxes behind labels are rectangles; the spring inside the magnifier is clipped a little less.
* Macro versions: layout and scale are physfig's own (not pixel copies). Specific gaps are listed per figure above and in the coverage table in `OPTIONS.md` (e.g. several objects in a row on the pulley table/ramp, wave axis end labels/arrow ends, the site's default motion-segment values, symmetric offset of parallel FBD forces, circuit mirror is experimental).
* `tikz_snippets` rely on the colour definitions and `\pffs` font macro in the standalone header.
